subject: Private deployment — custodian / escrow trigger proposal and insurance carve-outs
messages:
From: Claire Hsu <claire@medtech.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medtech.io>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment questions — custody, escrow triggers, and insurance

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed. Before we proceed to commercial approval we need some clarity on three items for our legal and IT risk review for an on‑prem deployment:

1) Custodian / access: we need a concise description of what operator access looks like post‑deployment (roles, minimum privileges, how credentials are stored). Our security team is insisting on an explicit clause that describes operator access boundary and an attestation cadence.

2) Escrow-like / snapshot access: our counsel prefers a mechanism to obtain an encrypted snapshot and minimal recovery keys in a limited set of trigger events (insolvency, material breach of SLA, sustained data loss). They call this an "escrow trigger"; would Redwood accept language around custodial snapshot delivery under specific triggers and an independent custodian process?

3) Insurance and indemnity carve-outs: given this will host regulated patient data (de‑identified but still in scope), we need to understand Redwood's cyber insurance limits and whether there are carve-outs tied to operator conduct.

Attached: MedTech_initial_RFI.pdf with their template questions.

Can you loop in legal and engineering so we can understand a negotiable starting point? We are under a board review deadline next Friday, so an initial position this week would be ideal.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Hsu
Head of IT Risk, MedTech Solutions

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Claire Hsu <claire@medtech.io>, Procurement <procurement@medtech.io>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — custody, escrow triggers, and insurance

Folks — looping you in per Claire's ask. Quick context: MedTech is a mid‑market healthcare SaaS customer leaning to an on‑prem deployment in their Azure stack. They want explicit language for: operator access boundary + attestation cadence, an escrow‑style snapshot delivery on narrowly defined triggers, and clarity on cyber insurance scopes.

Aditya — can you draft a short engineering summary describing operator roles (Operator, Readonly Support, Emergency Recovery), where keys are stored (KMS, HSM options), and our standard attestation cadence (quarterly/annual) and evidence we can provide (audit logs, access transcripts)? Keep it high level but precise — they will push.

Lauren — legal: they asked whether we can agree to a custodial snapshot delivery mechanism that includes an independent escrow custodian (not Redwood). We historically resist permanent data handover, but we have done encrypted snapshots + split key escrow under strict trigger language. Need your recommended redline bullets that preserve limits on scope (no ongoing operational control, one‑time transfer on verified trigger) and carve out operator conduct from insurance triggers.

Marissa — FYI for sales — this is in the later stage of the PO pipeline (DEAL-2027-037). I'll consolidate positions and propose a short statement for the order form addendum. Deadline: EOD Friday for an initial position; if not possible, Monday morning.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Claire Hsu <claire@medtech.io>, Procurement <procurement@medtech.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — custody, escrow triggers, and insurance

Karthik / team — initial legal position below. Drafting a short redline bundle (attached as redlines_v0.docx) but summarizing here so we can align quickly: 

1) Operator access boundary and attestation
- We will define permitted Redwood operator roles limited to diagnostics and emergency recovery. No persistent read access to customer application data unless explicitly authorized in writing.
- Operators will be constrained to ephemeral sessions recorded via session manager; session recordings, MFA logs, and justifications will be provided as part of quarterly attestation.
- Attestation cadence: quarterly summary statements of operator activity; detailed logs will be produced within 10 business days on reasonable request and subject to our data export process.

2) Escrow‑style snapshot delivery (proposal)
- Redwood will agree to produce an encrypted snapshot of the deployed instance and provide split recovery keys to an independent third‑party custodian only upon a narrowly defined trigger: (a) Redwood insolvency (bankruptcy filing), (b) Redwood material and uncured breach of the MSA for 60 days following written notice, or (c) prolonged and verified data unavailability for greater than 7 consecutive days despite commercially reasonable remediation efforts.
- The snapshot mechanism is strictly one‑time delivery for recovery purposes. The customer is expressly prohibited from using any Redwood‑provided administrative tooling to obtain ongoing operational access beyond the snapshot.
- Transfer process: snapshot will be encrypted with a symmetric key; the symmetric key will be split into two shares (Shamir) with one share delivered to the customer and the other to the independent custodian. Custodian release procedure requires independent verification and cross‑party signoff per the custodian's standard operating procedures.
- Redwood will not transfer any production‑grade secrets (e.g., Redwood private model weights) that are not necessary for customer recovery. Scope limited to customer dataset, model inputs/outputs, and configuration necessary to resume operation.

3) Insurance and indemnity carve‑outs
- Redwood's cyber liability coverage: we will provide current certificate limits (policy number redacted) and will agree to carry coverage levels typical for enterprise on‑prem vendors (we will include the certificate in the folder).
- Carrier exclusions tied to customer misuse or malicious actions will be expressly carved out from coverage triggers. If the incident results from post‑delivery customer admin credential compromise, standard indemnity principles apply and coverage may be limited.

Open items / asks for engineering input:
- Aditya: confirm the technical feasibility and expected time to produce an encrypted snapshot and what elements we will exclude (e.g., model parameter blobs). Also confirm how long the snapshot creation may take and whether we can commit to an SLA for snapshot delivery window post‑trigger (we currently think 10–15 business days).
- Karthik / Marissa: commercial ask — do we require an additional one‑time fee for custodian handling and escrow services? We should propose a nominal fee and surface it in the order form addendum.

I'll attach the draft redline (redlines_v0.docx). If we can get engineering wording today, we can present this to MedTech tomorrow.

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_v0.docx (contains legal clause language + proposed trigger definitions)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Claire Hsu <claire@medtech.io>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — custody, escrow triggers, and insurance

Thanks — quick engineering read and proposed text for the order form addendum. High level: feasible with the constraints Lauren proposed. Notes below and suggested language snippet you can drop into the addendum.

Feasibility summary:
- Snapshot content: we can export customer tenant data, deployment configuration, and logs. We will exclude Redwood proprietary binaries and model weight files by default; for recovery we can include model artifacts only if the customer has a prior separate model licensing attachment.
- Key management: snapshot will be encrypted with AES‑256; keys generated at snapshot time. We support integration to customer KMS or Redwood KMS. For the split key flow we will hand over a key share to the independent custodian and one share to the customer.
- Timing: estimated time to produce a verified encrypted snapshot in a trigger event is 10–15 business days for a standard deployment (may be longer for custom infra). We'll include a qualified SLA in the addendum.
- Evidence: we can produce session recordings (redacted for PII), audit logs, and a short operator action summary as part of the attestation packet.

Proposed addendum snippet (engineering language):
"Redwood will produce a single, encrypted snapshot of the Customer's deployed instance upon satisfaction of a Custodial Release Trigger (as defined in Section X). The snapshot shall consist of: (i) Customer configuration and metadata necessary to restore the deployment, (ii) Customer provided data stored within the deployment, and (iii) operational logs generated by the deployment. Redwood proprietary model binaries and other Redwood‑owned artifacts are excluded unless otherwise licensed in writing. The snapshot will be encrypted with AES‑256; a key split will be performed using a standard secret‑sharing algorithm with one share held by the Customer and one share held by an independent custodian. Delivery of the snapshot and key share to the custodian shall occur within 15 business days of verified trigger activation, subject to reasonable operational constraints."
Commercial note: I support a nominal custodian handling fee — propose a one‑time administrative fee of USD 7,500 to cover snapshot verification and custodian coordination. Happy to revise.

If that looks good I can produce a short engineer‑friendly appendix describing artifacts included/excluded for the redline bundle.

—Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
